chunks: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man stole from the war booty—what is incumbent upon him? Is his hand to be cut off? He said: “It is to be considered how much of it would fall to his share. If what he took is less than his allotted share, he is given taʿzīr and the remainder of his due property is handed over to him. If he took the equivalent of what belongs to him, then nothing is upon him. But if he took an excess equal to the price of a shield—and that is a quarter of a dīnār—his hand is cut off.”

key_terms.الْمَغْنَمِ: war booty from which fighters may have an allotted share
key_terms.ثَمَنِ مِجَنٍّ: the price of a shield, used here as the threshold measure for theft
key_terms.رُبُعُ دِينَارٍ: a quarter of a dīnār, the stated minimum amount for applying the hadd
key_terms.عُزِّرَ: he is disciplinarily punished with taʿzīr, short of the fixed hadd penalty
key_terms.فَضْلًا: an excess beyond what is rightfully his
key_terms.قُطِعَ: his hand is cut off, meaning the hadd punishment for theft is carried out
key_terms.نَصِيبِهِ: his assigned portion or rightful share

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who steals from the war booty before it is distributed?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling for one who steals from the war booty before distribution. The ruling depends on whether the amount taken is less than, equal to, or greater than his rightful share, and the hadd of theft applies only when the excess reaches the minimum legal threshold.
